data.narrative:
Hermeus, a Series C frontier-tech company developing supersonic and hypersonic capabilities, was last valued at $1.0B post-money on $500M raised. The supersonic and hypersonic sector comprises a limited peer universe: two public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and one private peer (Boom Supersonic), reflecting the nascent and capital-intensive nature of this domain.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach. Given the sparse peer set in this sector—no same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum density thresholds—a peer-median multiple could not be reliably established without introducing distortion from unrelated sectors. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $1.0B last post-money valuation, implying a forward value of $1.7B. This reflects typical step-up patterns observed in venture progression from Series C toward later institutional rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B, with a median estimate of $1.7B. This range incorporates reasonable variance around the single applicable method but should be interpreted with the caveat that it rests on limited methodological diversity. The primary uncertainty stems from the absence of sufficient same-sector peer data; future comparables from Boom Supersonic's funding events or public market debuts in hypersonic technologies could materially refine this estimate. Capital intensity and timeline-to-revenue in frontier aerospace remain key valuation drivers not fully captured by stage mechanics alone.
